title: 1.2 TRADING MARKETS
summary: This chapter surveys how trading markets function, starting from a taxonomy of financial instruments — real assets, financial assets, and derivatives — before moving to the mechanics of positions, trades, and the contract types (spot, forward, futures, swap, option) that let participants transact across time. It contrasts exchange-based trading, with its standardization, anonymity, and margining, against bilateral OTC dealing under ISDA documentation, and explains structural features like basis, spreads, closing out, and credit protections such as CDS. A recurring thread is what sets energy apart from other financial markets: non-storability, locational fragmentation, inelastic supply and demand, and the resulting illiquidity, price volatility, and pricing opacity. The chapter also touches on the regulatory and economic backdrop — regulated versus deregulated markets, supply/demand laws, and institutions like the EIA and FERC — that shapes how these trading mechanisms operate in practice.
